modules.title: ISBD Foundations
objectives: Identify MARC tags, indicators, and subfields

lessons.why: Reviewers need to know that the record describes a resource, not the cataloger workflow.
lessons.how: Read tags, indicators, and subfields as structured evidence.
lessons.common_mistake: Treating punctuation as decoration instead of encoded display logic.
lessons.do_not_automate: Do not infer missing source-of-information facts.

lessons.why: The deterministic engine is intentionally narrow.
lessons.how: Use findings for punctuation-only changes and hand off authority, URL, coordinate, control, and local-policy fields.
lessons.common_mistake: Accepting AI advice as cataloging authority.
lessons.do_not_automate: Authority headings, URLs, control fields, complex structured notes, complex cartographic coordinates, and local-policy fields.

lessons.why: Safe review depends on comparing current value, expected value, rationale, severity, and patch target.
lessons.how: Confirm the rule, inspect the proposed replacement, apply, and undo in sandbox mode if needed.
lessons.common_mistake: Applying a patch to the right tag but wrong repeated subfield.

quiz.question: Where does the slash live in the baseline 245 title/responsibility convention?

answers.explanation: The baseline engine uses prefix-on-current for 245$c.
That is legacy guide text and does not match the engine.

scenario_records.description: Fix a 245 field with missing title/responsibility boundary punctuation.

modules.title: Applying Area Rules
objectives: Separate deterministic punctuation from cataloger judgment
Use AI only as advisory help

lessons.why: Title boundaries are common and visible.
lessons.common_mistake: Putting slash at the end of $b.
lessons.do_not_automate: Choosing title proper from ambiguous source data.

lessons.why: Edition abbreviations often end with meaningful periods.
lessons.how: Preserve abbreviation points and add prescribed punctuation only where needed.
lessons.do_not_automate: Deciding whether wording is an edition statement.

lessons.how: Apply terminal punctuation to simple scale/music/serial statements.

lessons.why: Publication boundaries drive common display punctuation.
lessons.how: Use the 264 second indicator for function and preserve publisher abbreviation periods.
lessons.common_mistake: Using the wrong 264 indicator for production/publication/distribution/manufacture/copyright function.

lessons.why: Physical descriptions frequently use abbreviation periods.

lessons.how: Patch transcribed 490/440 fields and hand off controlled 8XX headings.
Patch simple notes and hand off structured notes.

lessons.why: Identifiers should not carry sentence punctuation.
lessons.how: Remove terminal punctuation from identifier values.
lessons.common_mistake: Treating ISBN periods like note punctuation.

lessons.why: AI can explain punctuation and suggest LCC/LCSH candidates, but it cannot authorize record changes.
lessons.how: Treat AI output as advisory. Apply only punctuation-only patches that pass deterministic guardrails; review LCC/LCSH candidates against authority/cataloging policy before saving.
lessons.common_mistake: Letting AI rewrite descriptive data or bypass deterministic ISBD findings.
lessons.do_not_automate: Authoritative headings, URLs, local fields, control fields, source-of-information decisions, and any non-punctuation rewrite.

lessons.why: Supervisors must defend every automated change.
lessons.how: Trace finding code to rule rationale and ISBD coverage status.
lessons.common_mistake: Approving a fix without checking rule scope.

lessons.how: Compare current value, expected value, subfield index, and field context.

lessons.why: Local policy belongs in explicit local rules.
lessons.how: Use schema-valid punctuation-only checks with tests.
lessons.common_mistake: Writing broad regexes that alter headings.
lessons.do_not_automate: Authority, URL, control, and local fields by default.

lessons.why: JS and Perl engines must stay identical.
lessons.how: Run shared fixtures through both test runners before release.
